cues.en: Hi.
cues.zh: 大家好。

cues.en: Great to be here.
cues.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

cues.en: I'm a cardiologist,
cues.zh: 我是一名心脏病专家，

cues.en: but before that, I was an exercise enthusiast.
cues.zh: 但在那之前，我是个运动狂热爱好者。

cues.en: I've exercised, I'll bet, pretty much every day of my life.
cues.zh: 毫不夸张地说，我这辈子几乎每天都在运动。

cues.en: I had two grandfathers who were alcoholics,
cues.zh: 我的祖父和外祖父都有酗酒问题，

cues.en: But for me, my way of coping with life is exercise.
cues.zh: 但对我来说，排解生活压力的方式就是运动。

cues.en: When I'm nervous, or anxious,
cues.zh: 每当我感到紧张、焦虑，

cues.en: or tired, or happy, or sad, or whatever,
cues.zh: 或是疲惫、快乐、悲伤，无论怎样，

cues.en: I exercise if I have the time.
cues.zh: 只要有时间我就会运动。

cues.en: Sometimes even when I don't. You might have seen me in an airport waiting for a flight, running up the down escalator with my backpack on to kill twenty minutes.
cues.zh: 有时甚至没时间也硬要运动。你可能在机场见过我，等飞机时背着背包在向下的自动扶梯上反向跑，就为了消磨20分钟。

cues.en: But I always thought that exercise was the best thing for my heart,
cues.zh: 但我一直以为运动对我的心脏是最好的，

cues.en: and I think it's how I decided at age 15 I wanted to be a cardiologist, actually.
cues.zh: 我想这大概也是我15岁时就决定当一名心脏病专家的原因。

cues.en: But now that I'm 56, and
cues.zh: 但现在我已经56岁了，

cues.en: a lot of decades have gone by,
cues.zh: 几十年一晃而过，

cues.en: I've started to have a few
cues.zh: 我的心脏开始出现一些

cues.en: warning signs from my heart. A couple of years ago, I noticed this, and I got on a mission. I'm a research cardiologist,
cues.zh: 危险信号。几年前我注意到了这一点，便开启了一项探究。我是一名研究型心脏病专家，

cues.en: and I have a research fellow, and he and I have been working on this for the past couple of years. And with the help of some of the brightest cardiologists from around the country, we
cues.zh: 我带了一名博士后研究员，我们俩在过去几年一直在攻克这个问题。在全美一些顶尖心脏病学家的协助下，

cues.en: have to come to some startling new insights that seem to be emerging about exercise.
cues.zh: 我们发现了一些关于运动的惊人新认知。

cues.en: This made me think twice about my lifestyle,
cues.zh: 这让我不得不重新审视自己的生活方式，

cues.en: and I'm worried I may have made a lethal mistake.
cues.zh: 我很担心自己可能犯下了一个致命的错误。

cues.en: I hope it's not too late,
cues.zh: 但愿现在还不算太晚，

cues.en: but let me tell you the story.
cues.zh: 请允许我把这个故事讲给你们听。

cues.en: So, as I said, I've been exercising for a long time, but if we go back twenty five hundred years, there was a guy named Pheidippides, who ran the 26 miles from a battlefield near
cues.zh: 正如我刚才所说，我已经坚持运动很多年了。但如果回到两千五百年前，有个叫 Pheidippides 的人，他从靠近

cues.en: Marathon,
cues.zh: 马拉松的战场出发，

cues.en: Greece into Athens to proclaim the news about a momentous victory over the Persians. And when he arrived at the emperor's throne and said, victory is ours, he abruptly
cues.zh: 跑了26英里到达希腊雅典，去宣布战胜波斯人的重大捷报。当他赶到元首王座前喊出“我们胜利了”之后，突然

cues.en: collapsed and died.
cues.zh: 倒地猝死。

cues.en: Now, you may have heard that story before, but what you probably didn't know is Pheidippides was an accomplished runner. He'd been a Greek herald messenger his whole life.
cues.zh: 你也许听过那个故事，但你可能不知道的是，Pheidippides 还是一位很有成就的跑者。他一生都是希腊的传令信使。

cues.en: He ran a lot of miles every day. I'll bet he was the fittest guy in Athens the day he died.
cues.zh: 他每天跑很多英里。我敢打赌，他去世那天是雅典最强健的人。

cues.en: That's strange.
cues.zh: 这很奇怪。

cues.en: But now let's go forward two millennia
cues.zh: 但现在，让我们向前推进两千年

cues.en: or more. When the baby boomers
cues.zh: 甚至更久。当婴儿潮一代

cues.en: came of age, another boom happened, the running boom.
cues.zh: 长大成人时，又一场热潮出现了——跑步热潮。

cues.en: If exercise was good for you, as anybody could know, then more had to be better. And what was the ultimate test
cues.zh: 如果锻炼对你有好处——这谁都知道——那更多就一定更好。而终极考验

cues.en: of running endurance was a marathon. There was a
cues.zh: 跑步耐力的终极考验，就是马拉松。曾有一位

cues.en: physician who became famous back in the mid seventies by boldly proclaiming that if you could complete a marathon,
cues.zh: 医生在七十年代中期出名，因为他大胆宣称，如果你能跑完马拉松，

cues.en: you were immune to a heart attack.
cues.zh: 你就对心脏病发作免疫了。

cues.en: This urban myth
cues.zh: 这个都市传说

cues.en: actually still holds sway with a lot of physicians.
cues.zh: 实际上至今仍让许多医生深信不疑。

cues.en: One of my patients and friends is John. He's 68 now, but he's been running for forty five years. As he puts it, if he hasn't run 12 miles in a day, he felt like he was wimping out.
cues.zh: 我的一位病人兼朋友是 John。他现在 68 岁，但已经跑了四十五年。用他的话说，如果一天没跑够 12 英里，他就觉得自己在偷懒。

cues.en: When I saw him, he came in to see me, and I said, John, let's do a cardio scan on you. It's a CT scan, simple, non invasive, quick, high-tech scan of your heart. Your arteries, I'm sure, will be soft and supple, and clean and healthy.
cues.zh: 我见到他时，他来找我看病，我说：John，咱们给你做个心脏扫描吧。就是 CT 扫描，简单、无创、快速、高科技的心脏扫描。我敢肯定，你的动脉会柔软有弹性、干净又健康。

cues.en: So that's what a normal cardio scan should look like, no calcium whatsoever in these arteries.
cues.zh: 所以，正常的心脏扫描应该是这样，这些动脉里完全没有钙。

cues.en: His is over here. His score was 1,800.
cues.zh: 他的在这边。他的评分是 1,800。

cues.en: Anything above zero is abnormal. Anything above 400 is severe.
cues.zh: 高于零就不正常。高于400就是严重。

cues.en: his arteries are harder than his bones.
cues.zh: 他的动脉比骨头还硬。

cues.en: That can't be good.
cues.zh: 这可不是好事。

cues.en: And he doesn't have any other risk factors to speak of.
cues.zh: 而且他没什么其他可说的风险因素。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: in fact, people do die doing marathons,
cues.zh: 事实上，确实有人跑马拉松跑死了，

cues.en: but let's be realistic.
cues.zh: 但现实点说。

cues.en: If you look at the latest data, the risk is minuscule, one in a hundred thousand participants.
cues.zh: 看最新数据，风险微乎其微，十万名参赛者里才一个。

cues.en: I've gotten to be friends with a guy named Ambi Burford. Ambi won the Boston Marathon in 1968.
cues.zh: 我跟一个叫Ambi Burford的人成了朋友。Ambi在1968年赢了波士顿马拉松。

cues.en: He is currently editor in chief and has been a long time editor at large
cues.zh: 他目前是主编，长期担任资深编辑

cues.en: at Runner's World magazine.
cues.zh: 在《跑者世界》杂志。

cues.en: In conversations we've had in recent months, he's challenged me. If endurance extreme exercise is so bad, show me the bodies.
cues.zh: 近几个月我们的交谈中，他向我提出挑战。如果耐力极限运动这么糟糕，拿出尸体给我看。

cues.en: He's got a good point. One in a hundred thousand is pretty low risk,
cues.zh: 他说得有道理。十万分之一的风险相当低，

cues.en: but I'm not so worried about that. Running is supposed to add years to your life, and even life to your years.
cues.zh: 但我不太担心这个。跑步本该延年益寿，甚至让岁月更有活力。

cues.en: Could it be shortening your life expectancy?
cues.zh: 它会不会反而缩短你的预期寿命？

cues.en: I'm not worried about dropping in a race, I'm just trying to do the right thing. I'm a cardiologist, I'm in the business of finding out the ideal diet and lifestyle.
cues.zh: 我不担心比赛中猝死，我只是想做对的事。我是心脏病医生，我的工作就是找出理想的饮食和生活方式。

cues.en: I'm coming to the conclusion that running marathons and extreme endurance athletics
cues.zh: 我逐渐得出结论：跑马拉松和极限耐力运动

cues.en: do not fit into that recipe.
cues.zh: 并不符合那个配方。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: that being said, let me be clear about this.
cues.zh: 话虽如此，让我说清楚。

cues.en: There is no single step you can take in your life to ensure robust health and remarkable longevity than a habit of daily exercise.
cues.zh: 在你一生中，没有什么单一举措能比每天锻炼的习惯更能确保强健体魄和非凡长寿。

cues.en: Okay? And this is a study of over 400,000
cues.zh: 好吧？这是对超过 40 万名中国人的一项研究，

cues.en: Chinese that was just published within the last year. We published an editorial along with this afterwards.
cues.zh: 这项研究刚刚在过去一年内发表。之后我们还配套发表了一篇社论。

cues.en: But they found that vigorous exercise, this is all cause mortality reduction. The more reduction, the better.
cues.zh: 但研究发现，高强度运动可以降低全因死亡率。降低得越多，效果越好。

cues.en: And this is minutes of daily exercise. So ten, twenty, thirty minutes of daily exercise up. At 40 it starts plateauing, at 45 or 50,
cues.zh: 这里显示的是每日运动时长。所以，每天运动 10 分钟、20 分钟、30 分钟，效果逐步提升。到 40 分钟时开始趋于平台期，在 45 或 50 分钟时，

cues.en: you get a point for further,
cues.zh: 进一步增加所带来的收益，

cues.en: it plateaus, so further efforts
cues.zh: 会趋于平台期，因此继续增加运动量

cues.en: and time do not appear
cues.zh: 和时间，似乎并不能

cues.en: to convey further improvements in life expectancy.
cues.zh: 进一步提高预期寿命。

cues.en: Down here is
cues.zh: 下面这里是

cues.en: exercise,
cues.zh: 运动，

cues.en: light to moderate exercise, walking, housework, day to day, moving around. Just get off your seat, move around.
cues.zh: 轻度到中度运动，比如走路、做家务、日常活动。离开座位，动起来就好。

cues.en: More is better there. It's not quite as beneficial as vigorous
cues.zh: 在这里，运动越多越好。虽然它不像高强度

cues.en: exercise, but more is better.
cues.zh: 运动那么有益，但多运动总是更好。

cues.en: You can exercise all day, it seems, without getting yourself in trouble, if you keep it down.
cues.zh: 看起来，只要保持较低强度，你几乎可以整天运动，也不会给身体带来问题。

cues.en: One of my
cues.zh: 我心目中的一位

cues.en: heroes, if you'd say, I love evolutionary medicine. I think if you look in the world of nature, into our deep past, you can find the template
cues.zh: 英雄吧，我很喜欢进化医学。我认为，如果你观察自然界，回望我们遥远的过去，就能找到理想健康的模板，

cues.en: for ideal health, even in our modern world.
cues.zh: 即使是在现代社会也一样。

cues.en: Charles Darwin was wrong about one thing though, it's not the survival of the fittest.
cues.zh: 不过，Charles Darwin 有一点说错了：并不是适者生存。

cues.en: In fact, it's the survival of the moderately fit.
cues.zh: 事实上，是中等适应者生存。

cues.en: Okay? If the best you can do is walk one flight of stairs before have to rest, things are not looking good. It could be a bumpy ride in the next few years. Okay? On the other hand, if you can dance, or lightly swim, or if you can even jog six miles an hour, that's a ten minute mile. Come on, that's a pretty comfortable pace. Right?
cues.zh: 明白吗？如果你最多只能走上一层楼梯就必须休息，那情况不太妙。未来几年可能会很艰难。明白吗？另一方面，如果你能跳舞、轻松游泳，甚至能以每小时 6 英里的速度慢跑，也就是 10 分钟跑 1 英里。拜托，这个速度其实相当舒服，对吧？

cues.en: Your mortality plummets. And if you, after warming up on a treadmill, can achieve a speed of seven to seven and a half miles an hour, you're pretty much bulletproof
cues.zh: 你的死亡风险会骤降。而且如果你在跑步机上热身后，能达到每小时七到七点五英里的速度，那你基本就百毒不侵了

cues.en: when you look at outcomes. And in fact, further attainments
cues.zh: 从结果来看。事实上，进一步提升

cues.en: of peak fitness do not translate into
cues.zh: 峰值体能，并不会转化为

cues.en: further increases in life expectancy.
cues.zh: 预期寿命的进一步延长。

cues.en: Okay? It plateaus out.
cues.zh: 对吧？它会趋于平台。

cues.en: In fact, there's a little trend that maybe it might even go up a little bit.
cues.zh: 事实上，有个小趋势是，它甚至可能还会再高一点。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: an important concept is the dose makes the poison. It's true with a lot of things. If
cues.zh: 一个重要概念是：剂量决定毒性。很多事都是这样。如果

cues.en: we could come up with a pill that gave all the benefits that we got from exercise, I'd be looking for work.
cues.zh: 我们能发明一种药丸，带来运动的所有好处，那我就要失业了。

cues.en: In fact, exercise not only cuts your chance of premature death in half, but it reduces risk for heart disease, Alzheimer's, osteoporosis,
cues.zh: 事实上，运动不仅把你的早逝几率减半，还降低心脏病、阿尔茨海默病、骨质疏松症、

cues.en: depression. It is an amazing drug. But just like any drug,
cues.zh: 抑郁症的风险。它是一味神奇的药。但就像任何药物，

cues.en: there is an ideal dose range. If you don't take enough of it, you don't get the benefit. If you take too much of it, it could be harmful,
cues.zh: 都有一个理想剂量范围。摄入不够，就得不到好处。摄入太多，可能有害，

cues.en: maybe even
cues.zh: 甚至可能

cues.en: fatal.
cues.zh: 致命。

cues.en: When you're sitting here,
cues.zh: 当你坐在这里，

cues.en: listening, sitting around like most Americans spend most of their day sitting, doing nothing, your heart's pumping, just idling along about
cues.zh: 听着，像大多数美国人一天中大部分时间那样坐着无所事事，你的心脏在泵血，只是怠速运转，大约

cues.en: a gallon a minute, about four or five liters a minute. If we went out, went for run right now, and you ran hard, that would go up four, five, six folds,
cues.zh: 每分钟一加仑，约每分钟四到五升。如果我们现在出去跑，而且跑得很猛，那会提高四、五、六倍，

cues.en: six, five, six gallons a minute.
cues.zh: 每分钟六、五、六加仑。

cues.en: That's
cues.zh: 那才是

cues.en: a workout. Your heart is working hard. But that's what it's meant to do intermittently,
cues.zh: 一次锻炼。你的心脏在努力做功。但这正是它应该间歇性做的事情，

cues.en: you know, maybe a few minutes, five, ten, maybe thirty minutes, maybe up to sixty minutes, but by sixty minutes something starts happening.
cues.zh: 你知道，也许几分钟、五到十分钟，也许三十分钟，最多六十分钟，但到六十分钟时，有些事情就开始发生了。

cues.en: The stretch in the chamber starts overwhelming
cues.zh: 心腔受到的牵拉开始压垮

cues.en: the
cues.zh: 心肌

cues.en: muscles' ability to adapt, catecholamine levels, the adrenaline levels rise, the free radicals blossom, and it starts burning the heart, it starts searing and inflaming the inside of your coronary arteries.
cues.zh: 的适应能力，儿茶酚胺水平、肾上腺素水平升高，自由基大量涌现，开始灼烧心脏，开始灼烧冠状动脉内壁并引发炎症。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: we're not really meant for these sustained levels of exercise
cues.zh: 我们其实并不适合长时间维持这种强度的运动

cues.en: hours at a time. If you go to a marathon,
cues.zh: 一跑就是几个小时。去跑马拉松的话，

cues.en: this has been done several times, you take a troponin level at the end of the marathon, over half of them will have elevated troponins. What's a troponin? Troponin is a sacred chemical to us cardiologists.
cues.zh: 有人做过好几次这样的研究：在马拉松结束后测肌钙蛋白，超过一半的选手肌钙蛋白都会升高。肌钙蛋白是什么？对我们心脏病医生来说，肌钙蛋白是一种神圣的化学物质。

cues.en: When we see a troponin goes up, it means one thing: heart muscle has died. Normally, we hop into action because that generally means there's a heart attack going on, we need to get a vessel open. In this case, these are little micro tears from the stretching and the searing.
cues.zh: 看到肌钙蛋白升高，只意味着一件事：心肌坏死了。通常我们会立刻行动，因为这一般意味着正在发生心肌梗死，需要尽快打通血管。但这里的肌钙蛋白升高，是牵拉和灼烧造成的微小撕裂。

cues.en: And it's not a big deal if you do it once, these are little mining micro tears. They heal, a few days later it's gone, the heart's
cues.zh: 偶尔一次没什么大碍，这些只是微小的撕裂。它们会愈合，几天后就恢复了，心脏

cues.en: back down to normal size. But you do this over and over again,
cues.zh: 也回到正常大小。但如果一次又一次地这样做，

cues.en: and the chambers start dialing up. They get scarred, they get stiff, they get thickened.
cues.zh: 心腔就会开始扩大。它们会留下疤痕、变得僵硬、增厚。

cues.en: If
cues.zh: 如果

cues.en: you look closely, you can see these little white patches in these veteran extreme endurance athletes that accumulate
cues.zh: 仔细观察，你能在这些资深极限耐力运动员身上看到这些小白斑，它们会不断累积

cues.en: in people who've been doing this for years and decades. Their heart becomes
cues.zh: 在坚持了几年、几十年的人身上。他们的心脏会

cues.en: older before it's time. We're asking too much of it. It's overwhelming
cues.zh: 未老先衰。我们对它的要求太高了，已经超出

cues.en: the heart's capacities.
cues.zh: 心脏的承受能力。

cues.en: And this is a fascinating study done by a cardiologist that I know, and his son who's also a cardiologist, these were both avid runners up in Minnesota. They did a study looking at the CT scans, like I showed you of John's. They looked at a group of
cues.zh: 我认识的一位心脏病学家和他同样是心脏病学家的儿子做了一项非常有趣的研究，他们都是明尼苏达州热爱跑步的人。他们做了一项研究，查看像我给你看的约翰那样的 CT 扫描，他们观察了一组

cues.en: marathoners who had been doing this for at least twenty five years, at least 25 marathons during that time, compared to sedentary controls. And you can see here, they had 62% more plaque despite
cues.zh: 那些坚持跑步至少二十五年、期间至少跑过 25 次马拉松的老将，与久坐不动的对照组相比。你可以看到，他们的斑块反而多了 62%，尽管……

cues.en: fewer risk factors.
cues.zh: 更少的风险因素。

cues.en: People say that can't be true. In fact, a German cardiologist just replicated this study showing in 108 marathoners similar findings.
cues.zh: 人们说那不可能是真的。事实上，一位德国心脏病专家刚刚重复了这项研究，在108名马拉松选手身上得到了类似结果。

cues.en: Hard to dismiss.
cues.zh: 很难反驳。

cues.en: Veteran endurance athletes also have about a five fold increased risk of atrial fibrillation,
cues.zh: 资深耐力运动员患心房颤动的风险也会增加约五倍，

cues.en: a dangerous irregular heart rhythm. There's sort of an
cues.zh: 一种危险的不规则心律。有点像一种

cues.en: epidemic of this going on among
cues.zh: 这种现象在……中蔓延

cues.en: runners because
cues.zh: 运行器，因为

cues.zh: 他

cues.zh: 脱离了美国主流社会，搬到墨西哥北部铜峡谷的塔拉乌马拉印第安人聚居区生活。他是一位传奇的

cues.zh: 当地的印第安人因他惊人的耐力给他起外号叫 Caballo Blanco，即“白马”。可惜的是，Micah True 去世了，

cues.zh: 这是其中一篇，作者是我的同事兼挚友 Chip LaVie。

cues.zh: 平均追踪了15年，最长达30年。他们对比了不跑步的人和跑者——跑者有1.4万人，不跑步的有3.8万人。

cues.zh: 有趣的是，

cues.zh: 好吧，事实上

She did 10 races last year, she's 30. She won half of them. The other half, she collapsed in heat exhaustion, dangerous heat exhaustion near the end of the race. I told Megan,
cues.zh: 我的一个好朋友，梅根·纽科默（Megan Newcomer），是来自纽约市的铁人三项运动员。她就在隔壁长大。她是我们家的挚友。她是全国顶尖的铁人三项运动员之一。她去年参加了10场比赛，今年30岁。她赢了一半。另一半比赛中，她在接近终点时因中暑而倒下，那是极其危险的热衰竭。我对梅根说，

cues.zh: 梅格，如果你想

cues.zh: 参加真正的奥运会——你完全有这个可能——你只要继续刻苦训练，或许再提升一下水平。但如果你想保持健康，

cues.zh: 能够活到

This replicated those same findings we saw on Micah Tru and these other findings I've been telling you about. But what provides hope to me is that when they took these guys off their iron mouse training regimens,
cues.zh: 研究人员狠狠地折磨了这些小鼠。他们让小鼠每天精疲力竭地奔跑，持续了四个月。你知道吗？这复制了我们在米卡·特鲁（Micah Tru）身上看到的那些发现，以及我刚才告诉你的其他发现。但让我看到希望的是，当研究人员停止这些“铁人小鼠”的魔鬼训练计划后，

cues.zh: 它们的心脏恢复了正常。纤维化甚至消退了，它们的心室

cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.zh: 我现在会缩短跑步距离。跑步时，我跑1.5英里，最多3英里，通常在2英里左右。而且我把

cues.zh: 像我这样的人，根本不想听这套说法。其实他们有点想迁怒于报信的人。我一直收到很多关于这项研究的负面评论，但你知道我决定怎么做吗？就是在锻炼这件事上，你需要舒服地待在 U 型曲线中段的安全区，
